chip: Hailo-8 (Hailo M.2 M-key module HM218B1C2FAE, s/n HLLWM2B233704039, CM5 IO Board rev 2 M.2 slot, PCIe Gen3 x1)
host: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 Rev 1.0 on CM5 IO Board rev 2, aarch64, Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.18.39+rpt-rpi-2712

bootloader.note: M.2 slot 3.3V buck is gated by the CM5 PCIE_PWR_EN pin (R14 pulls EN to GND, default OFF); a current bootloader plus PCIE_PROBE=1 is the known-good firmware state. Initial link-down was mechanical: reseating the module restored the link.

model.hef: model.hailo8.hef (Hailo Model Zoo all_minilm_l6_v2, v2.19.0, INT8)
model.front_end: word (raw word-embedding gather; position/token-type/LayerNorm inside the HEF; additive -1e4 attention mask input)

command: cargo test -p turboembed --features hailo --test hailo_minilm -- --include-ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 && cargo run -p turboembed --features hailo --release --example hailo_bench

quality.note: Values are digit-identical to pi5-hailo8.json: the same INT8 HEF reproduces bitwise across hosts (Pi 5 AI HAT+ and CM5IO M.2), so quality deltas between lanes can only come from the HEF, not the host.

performance.note: HEF is batch-1 with a fixed 128-token frame, so throughput is flat in text length and batch rows loop on the host. CM5 matches the Pi 5 lane to the microsecond at p50 (HEF-bound, same Gen3 x1 link). hailortcli run reports 75.45 FPS steady state on the same HEF (random data).
